systems.name: Grid Substation & Medium-Voltage Switchgear
systems.purpose: The Grid Substation system is the primary point of entry for utility power (11 kV–138 kV). It steps voltage down to site medium voltage (MV, 11 kV) for distribution to all power pods. The P&ID boundary encompasses utility demarcation point → incoming overhead/underground cable → MV Gas-Insulated Switchgear (GIS) → protective relays → MV busbar → feeder circuits to downstream transformers.[1][2]

systems.name: Power Transformers (MV/LV Distribution)
systems.purpose: Step MV (11 kV) down to low voltage (LV 415 V / 480 V) for data hall pods. Each transformer is a cast-resin dry-type unit serving one power distribution board (PDB) per pod pair. Boundary: MV feeder cable from MV-SWG-01 → transformer primary terminals → transformer secondary → LV switchgear (SYS-6).[2][3]

systems.name: UPS — Double-Conversion Modular Chain
systems.purpose: Provides conditioned, uninterruptible AC power to data hall PDUs. A distributed block redundant topology (typically 4-to-3 or 2N) ensures any single UPS module failure does not interrupt load. Boundary: LV input from transformer/LV switchgear → UPS rectifier → battery string → inverter → UPS bypass switch → output busbar → downstream PDUs.[1][2][3]

systems.name: Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS) & Static Transfer Switches (STS)
systems.purpose: ATS transfers loads between utility source and generator output during utility failure (transfer time ~10–30 s). STS provides sub-cycle (<4 ms) transfer between two UPS output buses. Boundary: Generator output bus → ATS input A; Utility bus → ATS input B; ATS output → UPS input.[2][3]

systems.name: Diesel Backup Generators
systems.purpose: Last-resort electrical generation. Multiple large-frame generator sets configured N+1. Engine management via integral ECU (EMCP/Woodward); paralleling via dedicated generator paralleling controller. Boundary: Fuel tank → fuel system → engine → alternator → generator output breaker → paralleling busbar → ATS input.[1][2][3]

systems.name: Low-Voltage Distribution Switchgear & Electrical Power Monitoring
systems.purpose: Distributes LV (415 V) power from transformers to UPS inputs, PDU feeds, mechanical plant, and auxiliary loads. Includes intelligent circuit breakers with EPMS integration. Boundary: Transformer LV secondary → LV main switchboard → distribution circuits → UPS inputs, CRAH panels, mechanical plant panels.[1][2]

systems.name: Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)
systems.purpose: Grid-forming or grid-following BESS provides extended backup, demand response, and real-time frequency/voltage support for AI load transients. Deployed at MV or LV with a power conversion system (PCS/inverter). Boundary: BESS enclosure → PCS → MV/LV bus connection → site microgrid EMS.[1][2][3]

systems.name: Rack-Level Power Distribution (PDU / rPDU)
systems.purpose: Distributes power at rack level from UPS output to individual IT equipment outlets. Intelligent switched rPDUs provide per-outlet monitoring and remote switching. Boundary: UPS/STS output → row-level distribution board → A+B rPDU feeds → individual server/switch outlets.[2][3]

systems.name: Primary Cooling Loop — Facility Water System (FWS)
systems.purpose: Closed hydronic FWS loop: chilled water produced at centrifugal/magnetic-bearing chillers (7°C supply) → primary pumps → CDU heat exchanger primary side → CRAH/RDHx coils → return to chiller (12–14°C return). Condenser loop: chiller condensers → cooling towers → return.[2][3]

systems.name: Technology Cooling System (TCS) — CDU & Secondary Loop
systems.purpose: Isolated secondary liquid cooling loop for direct-to-chip (D2C) GPU/CPU cold plates. CDU provides liquid-to-liquid heat exchange between FWS primary loop (7°C facility water) and TCS secondary loop (32°C supply to servers, 40°C return). Boundary: CDU facility-side inlet (from FWS) → BPHE → CDU secondary outlet → rack supply manifold → cold plates → rack return manifold → CDU secondary inlet.[2][3]

systems.name: Compute Rack — Representative Sample (RCK-01)
systems.purpose: Single OCP Open Rack v3 (ORv3) or equivalent 48U cabinet representing the IT compute layer. Contains GPU/AI compute nodes with direct-to-chip liquid cooling (cold plates + OCP UQD manifolds) and dual-feed rPDUs. Boundary: Rack cabinet → IT equipment → cold plate manifolds → rPDU outlets → network patch panel.[2][3]

systems.name: Building Management System (BMS) & DCS Integration
systems.purpose: Supervisory control, monitoring, and automation of all facility mechanical systems (HVAC, cooling, power). Acts as the integration layer between field devices (Zone 3) and enterprise/DCIM platforms (Zone 0). Boundary: All DDC/PLC field I/O → BMS server → DCIM integration bus → enterprise systems.[1][2][3]

systems.name: DCIM — Vertiv Environet & Next Predict
systems.purpose: Centralized Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) providing real-time power, thermal, and asset visibility across the entire facility. Next Predict adds AI-based predictive maintenance on top of Environet telemetry. Boundary: All SNMP/BACnet/Modbus endpoints → Environet collectors → DCIM dashboard → Next Predict cloud API.[4][5][6][7][8]

systems.name: Network Fabric — Spine-Leaf & Firewalls
systems.purpose: Two-tier Clos spine-leaf IP fabric for data-plane east-west traffic. Perimeter firewalls provide north-south segmentation. OT network (BMS/DCIM) is isolated by Moxa industrial firewalls. Boundary: ToR switches per rack → leaf switches → spine switches → border firewalls → internet peering / cloud interconnect.[1][2][3]

systems.name: Out-of-Band (OOB) Management — KVM & Serial Console
systems.purpose: Dedicated out-of-band management plane providing serial console and KVM-over-IP access to all servers, switches, and infrastructure equipment when the primary network is unavailable. Boundary: Dedicated OOB Ethernet switch → ACS 8000 console servers → serial ports of all managed devices; KVM-over-IP → server video/keyboard/mouse.[9][10][11][12]

systems.name: Fire Detection, Alarm & Suppression
systems.purpose: Multi-layer fire detection (VESDA aspirating + conventional detectors) → FACP → two-zone cross-confirmation → clean agent suppression (Novec 1230). EPO integrated. Boundary: Smoke detectors / VESDA throughout data halls and electrical rooms → FACP → suppression release → agent distribution nozzles. All safety-hardwired; BMS receives alarm status read-only.[1][2][3]

systems.name: Physical Security — CCTV, Access Control & Perimeter
systems.purpose: Multi-layer electronic physical security: perimeter detection → mantrap access control → CCTV surveillance → alarm management. All critical zone access requires multi-factor authentication. Boundary: Perimeter PIDS sensors → access control panels → door hardware → biometric readers → CCTV cameras → VMS server → security operations center (SOC).[1][2][3]

systems.name: HVAC — Computer Room, Electrical Room & Battery Room Ventilation
systems.purpose: General HVAC and critical ventilation for non-IT spaces: electrical switchgear rooms (minimum 35°C setpoint), battery rooms (H₂ dilution ventilation), generator rooms (combustion air + exhaust), and office/NOC spaces. Boundary: AHU inlet → filter → coil → supply fan → distribution ductwork → space → return/exhaust.[2][3]

instrument_loops.name: Overcurrent Protection
instrument_loops.description: CT (TT-MV-01) → 1A secondary → PRO-RLY-01 (pickup set at 1.2× FLA, time-overcurrent I²T curve) → hardwired trip output → MV-SWG-01 breaker trip coil. Cross-trips peer relay PRO-RLY-02 via IEC 61850 GOOSE within <4 ms.

instrument_loops.name: Arc Flash Detection
instrument_loops.description: Optical fiber arc-flash sensors within MV-SWG-01 busbar cells → direct hardwired arc flash detect input → PRO-RLY-01 → high-speed trip (<8 ms) → breaker trip coil.

instrument_loops.name: EPO
instrument_loops.description: EPO-BTN-01 (key-switch + dual-break) → hardwired supervised loop → shunt trip coil MV-SWG-01. Operates independently of BMS/SCADA software.

instrument_loops.name: Chilled Water Supply Temperature Control
instrument_loops.description: TT-FWS-01 (7°C setpoint) → CHL-CTL-A → chiller compressor speed modulation via OptiView PID loop → maintain evaporator leaving water at 7 ± 0.5°C.

instrument_loops.name: Pump Differential Pressure Control
instrument_loops.description: PT-FWS-01 → BMS DDC-01 PID loop → PMP-VFD-01 speed signal → CHW-PMP-01 speed → maintain system ΔP at remote header ≥1.5 bar.

instrument_loops.name: Isolation on Chiller Fault
instrument_loops.description: CHL-CTL-A alarm → BMS-SRV command → FCV-FWS-01 close (chiller isolation) → standby chiller FCV opens → N+1 maintained.

instrument_loops.name: Legionella / Water Treatment
instrument_loops.description: WTS-PLC-01 timer + conductivity probe → dosing pump command → biocide injection into condenser loop.

appendices.appendix: SYS-1 — System 1: Grid Substation & Medium-Voltage Switchgear

rows.Detail: ≥1 live MV feeder; ≥1 protection relay per circuit armed; EPO circuit continuous supervision
Category I — Catastrophic (loss of both utility feeds → full site blackout)[1][3]
Arc flash (NFPA 70E boundary); SF6 gas release (GIS maintenance); out-of-phase closing; cyber-induced false trip of protection relay[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
SIL 3 (protection relay trip function); SL-T 4 (substation zone)[1][2]
N+1 transformer arrangement per distribution zone; winding temperature monitoring active; cooling fans operational
Category I — Catastrophic (transformer failure eliminates power to affected pod)[3]
Arc flash (LV side); winding overheat; thermal sensor spoofing blocking fan actuation; cascading overload on redundant unit[1]
SIL 1 (thermal protection); SL-T 2 (field zone)[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-3 — System 3: UPS — Double-Conversion Modular Chain

rows.Detail: ≥N+1 UPS modules online; battery autonomy ≥5 min at full load; static bypass operable
Category I — Catastrophic (all modules fail); Category II — single module (N+1 intact)[3]
Li-ion thermal runaway; bypass failure; RCE on NMC3 card (TLStorm class CVE) enabling simultaneous module shutdown; out-of-phase bypass transfer[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
SIL 2 (bypass/BMS); SL-T 3 (Zone 2 Electrical)[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-4 — System 4: Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS) & Static Transfer Switches (STS)

rows.Detail: 1 ATS per distribution circuit; transfer complete within 30 s of utility failure; STS <4 ms
Category I — Catastrophic (misoperation causes sustained power loss or arc flash)[3]
Out-of-phase transfer (mechanical damage to generators); failure to transfer; command injection via Modbus write[1]
≥N+1 generators; start within 30 s of utility loss; day tank ≥8-hour fuel at rated load; paralleling within 5 s of voltage matching
Category I — Catastrophic (all generators fail); Category II — single unit (N+1 intact)[3]
Fuel spill/fire; exhaust CO accumulation; out-of-phase paralleling (shaft damage, arc flash); governor manipulation via CAN/Modbus[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
SIL 2 (paralleling / auto-start); SL-T 2–3[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-6 — System 6: Low-Voltage Distribution Switchgear & Electrical Power Monitoring

rows.Detail: 2N LV switchboard configuration; EPMS metering active on all critical feeders
Category I (main bus fault); Category II (individual feeder)[3]
LV arc flash; breaker trip curve manipulation via Modbus write; telemetry masking hiding transformer overload[1]

appendices.appendix: SYS-7 — System 7: Battery Energy Storage System (BESS)

rows.Detail: ≥1 BESS unit at ≥80% SoC; off-gas detection active; fire suppression armed
Category I — Catastrophic (BESS fire / thermal runaway); Category II — BMS fault[3]
Li-ion thermal runaway; HF off-gas; BMS override → continuous overcharge → cell swelling; cyber manipulation of SoC data masking unsafe condition[1]
~$5.0M per hour (throttled compute)[1]
SIL 2 (BMS thermal runaway protection); SL-T 3[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-9 — System 9: Primary Cooling Loop — Facility Water System (FWS)

rows.Detail: ≥N+1 chillers; CHW supply ≤14°C; N+1 primary CHW pumps; water treatment dosing continuous
Category I — Catastrophic (total chiller loss → IT thermal trip within minutes)[3]
Refrigerant release (R-1234ze, R-134a); Legionella (cooling tower); condensing loop failure → chiller high-pressure trip; VFD firmware corruption halting CHW flow[1]
~$5.0M per hour (throttled to $12.5M on full loss)[1]
SIL 1 (chiller high-pressure protection); SL-T 2[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-10 — System 10: Technology Cooling System (TCS) — CDU & Secondary Loop

rows.Detail: ≥N+1 CDU pumps; secondary supply ≤18°C; leak detection armed; DI conductivity <1 µS/cm
Category I — Catastrophic (CDU pump stop → GPU thermal trip in 45–60 s)[1][3]

Coolant leak onto IT hardware (electrical short); pump cavitation; PLC firmware bricking via network; DPT manipulation causing low-flow condition; coordinated ransomware disabling all CDUs simultaneously[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
SIL 2 (leak isolation, thermal runaway prevention); SL-T 3[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-12 — System 12: Building Management System (BMS) & DCS Integration

rows.Detail: ≥1 BMS server active; all safety I/O polled ≤5 s; BMS VLAN isolated from enterprise IT
Category I — Catastrophic (BMS compromise enables global setpoint manipulation → facility-wide trip)[1][3]
Exploitation of unpatched RCE (Niagara CVE, CVSS 9.8); BMS-to-FACP bridge abuse triggering false suppression; unauthorized write to cooling setpoints via Modbus[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
BMS supervisory not SIL-rated; safety I/O functions SIL 1; SL-T 3[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-16 — System 16: Fire Detection, Alarm & Suppression

rows.Detail: All VESDA detectors sampling; FACP armed all zones; suppression cylinders charged; EPO circuit supervise-enabled
Category I — Catastrophic (FACP failure → undetected fire; false suppression → compute loss + O₂ hazard)[1][3]

Undetected incipient fire; false suppression discharge (O₂ asphyxiation hazard in sealed room); BMS-to-FACP network bridge exploited to inject false confirmation codes triggering suppression and EPO; Li-ion thermal runaway off-gas (HF)[1]
~$12.5M per hour[1]
SIL 3 (suppression release / EPO); SL-T 3[1][2]

appendices.appendix: SYS-17 — System 17: Physical Security — CCTV, Access Control & Perimeter

rows.Detail: 100% perimeter and critical zone camera coverage; all access control panels battery-backed; PIDS active
Category II — Critical (CCTV loss = security blind spots; ACS failure = physical access breach)[3]

CCTV compromise (VAPIX CVE-2025-0324 privilege escalation → video stream access)[1]; Mercury LP1502 buffer overflow (CVE-2022-31481) → root shell → all mantraps unlocked[1]; PIDS defeat enabling physical access to MV switchgear or generators
Not SIL-rated; SL-T 2–3[1][2]
